body.x: Clips Tech (President James Lee, www.clip-s.co.kr) exhibited its bluetooth headset, the NeckBand series, at CES 2015, which runs Jan. 6-9 in Las Vegas.

The NeckBand series is outdoor-friendly headsets worn around the neck. A person can make and receive phone calls and enjoy various multi-media functions without inserting the earphones directly into his or her ears. While the earphones can be used, the product’s built-in speakers give the freedom to make phone calls while biking, hiking, or driving by simply wearing the headset around the neck.

Apt-x Codec and the 20㎐~22㎑ transmission of audible frequencies yield crystal clear sounds, while the voice alert system, in cases of low battery or bluetooth pairing with the power, allows convenience. Moreover, the headset is almost weightless when placed around a person’s neck as it only weighs 27g.

The battery lasts for a maximum standby time of 700 hours and 20 hours of continuous usage. Music can be played non-stop for up to 18 hours. The bluetooth connection range is about 10 meters, and the headset vibrates when out of range, thus preventing misplacement of the connected mobile phone.

Since its founding in 2009, Clips Tech has been developing and manufacturing bluetooth products, such as digital voice recorder, hearing aid, special camcorder, bluetooth pen, and wearable devices (ie. Neck Band, N-Watch).

Held annually in January and owned and produced by the Consumer Electronics Association (CEA), CES 2015 is the world's largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition to see the latest global trends in consumer electronics industry in one spot.

Globally recognized for its record in the number of published articles for CES, AVING News has been sending its reporters to CES every year to deliver the fastest and freshest news on the spot. This year, AVING News is using smartphones for news reporting, in line with the trend of one-person media.
